LESSON: INDEPENDENT SIGN READING - GRADE APPROPRIATE TEXT

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.1: Independent Sign reading - Grade Appropriate Text
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Independent Sign reading - Grade Appropriate Text, part of Strand 2 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to read/ sign read different types of materials?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Independent Sign reading - Grade Appropriate Text together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to learn: Learners organises own work as they take place in selecting reading materials

• Critical thinking and problem solving : Learners develop a good reading culture by engaging in different activities such as

creating chain stories, forming a book club etc.

• Self-efficacy Learner develop self awareness and planning skills as they create a reading log

Values:
● Responsibility is inculcated as the learner searches for reading materials, reads, and keeps a reading log

Link to other subjects

All subjects require intensive and extensive reading

Suggested Learning Resources:

digital devices, online fiction and non-fiction texts, adapted course books for learners with Hearing Impairment, charts,
